A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with readable main text, figures, equations and appendices. Pages 2–30 have identical text and rendered images; v4 adds Appendix C.6 and changes first-page publication formatting.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original synthetic Transformer experiments comparing ARM and EBM convergence, logit distances and KL divergence in Figures 2–5.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds learning-rate sensitivity and gradient-noise results in Appendix C.6, Figures 6–8.

M1.justification: The ARM and EBM definitions, bijective mappings, training objectives and Transformer implementations are unchanged. C.6 evaluates the existing model classes without introducing a method component.

E1.justification: The reported coverage remains synthetic sequence modeling with Zipfian and softargmax-normal distributions and the vocabulary/length configurations in C.2. C.6 adds optimization diagnostics without identifying a new dataset, domain or task.

E2.justification: All retained comparisons are unchanged, and Figures 6–8 continue comparing EBMs with ARMs. No additional comparison method is evaluated.

E3.justification: C.1 retains the original three-rate search and selected-rate reporting. New C.6 evaluates nine learning rates from 0.00001 to 0.1 and introduces gradient noise scale, gradient coherence and coordinate-wise SNR measurements. These are added protocols; the retained experiments' settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: C.6 adds a substantive investigation of optimization robustness: learning-rate sensitivity in Figures 6–7 and mini-batch gradient-noise behavior in Figure 8. These address questions absent from v3's model-size, sequence-configuration and distribution/logit-convergence analyses.

E5.justification: No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests are added. Figure 8 reports gradient variability as a diagnostic outcome, without adding uncertainty estimates for the experimental comparisons or explaining their statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Figures 2–5 remain identical. New Figure 6 places both models' best final losses at learning rate 0.01; C.6 reports slightly greater learning-rate robustness for ARMs and broadly similar gradient-noise sensitivity. These are additional findings, not revised performance under the retained settings.

T1.justification: The formal model definitions, bijection, equivalence-of-minima result, KL bounds and proofs in Appendices A–B are unchanged. Figure 8 supplies standard formulas explaining empirical gradient diagnostics without adding a theoretical construction, derivation or guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions concerning ARM–EBM equivalence, the soft Bellman connection, teacher forcing and distillation bounds. C.6 adds supporting evidence without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: C.6 frames its diagnostics as further confirmation of the already stated interpretation that ARMs can behave similarly to EBMs. It adds no distinct mechanism explanation or limitation; the conclusion's qualifications about optimization and approximation error remain identical.

D1.justification: Figure 7 documents the additional learning-rate values, and Figure 8 specifies the gradient-diagnostic formulas. Existing implementation details remain unchanged. C.6 does not identify its particular model/data configuration or mini-batch sampling details.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and bibliography are identical. C.6 introduces no citations or revised positioning relative to prior research.

P1.justification: v4 appends the short Optimization dynamics subsection with explanatory paragraphs and captions, and updates the publication footer and arXiv stamp. The existing narrative and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 adds a learning-rate summary plot, a nine-panel training-curve figure and a four-panel gradient-diagnostic figure. Existing Figures 1–5 and pages 2–30 retain their layout; the first page undergoes limited reflow.

improvement.justification: C.6 usefully supplements v3's selected-learning-rate comparisons with sensitivity tests and gradient-noise diagnostics while preserving the existing theory and results. This modestly strengthens the empirical discussion of optimization behavior. Missing configuration and mini-batch sampling details, together with absent run-level uncertainty reporting, limit the strength and reproducibility of the added evidence.
